text.p: Philippine oil refiner Petron Corp's nine-month results were disappointing and would lead to reductions in full-year earnings forecasts, market analysts said on Thursday.

Petron's 2.7 billion pesos ($102.66 million) nine-month net income reported on Wednesday was more than 30 percent above the 2.0 billion pesos ($76.04 million) it reported in the same period last year.
But analysts said the 1996 figure included some 1.3 billion pesos ($49.43 million) the refiner is claiming from the government-run Oil Price Stabilisation Fund (OPSF) but has not yet received.

"Adjusting for these figures, the company's sales would actually be up a mere 0.09 percent from last year's 39.12 billion pesos ($1.49 billion) and net income would be down 5.5 percent," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities Inc.

"Company officials confirmed that they included their claims from the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund in the nine month earnings. (But) even with that included, their profits are still below expectations," said Al Rillo, an analyst at DBS Securities Philippines Inc.

The government owes oil firms more than 2.0 billion pesos in reimbursements from the OPSF, a buffer fund that cushions domestic oil prices from fluctuations in crude costs and foreign exchange. Petron's claim against the fund is the biggest.
Officials of the oil refiner were unavailable for comment.
Analysts said they would reduce their full-year forecasts for Petron.

"The first three quarters net income was lower than our expectations. We are downgrading our full-year net income forecast from 4.4 billion pesos ($167.3 million) to 3.6-3.8 billion pesos ($136.88-144.48 million)," said Fritz Aclan, research head at Dharmala Securities (Philippines) Inc.
Analysts blamed Petron's lower net profit largely on an automatic oil price formula implemented in August as an interim step towards full deregulation next year.
The formula allows oil companies to adjust domestic oil prices on a monthly basis instead of once every two months. The formula is based on movements in Singapore Posted Prices instead of crude cost.
Oil refiners earlier said that the formula had failed to pass on increases in crude costs from an average of $17 a barrel in August to $22 this October.

"We no longer expect that they will meet our 4.8 billion peso ($182.51 million) year-end profit forecast. We will likely see year-end profits flat as a pancake against last year's 4.02 billion ($159.69 million)," Reyes said.
OCBC Securities Inc said it was also downgrading its 4.42 billion peso ($168.06 million) forecast to 4.02 billion.
"Definitely, it will not hit 10 percent growth in net income since as of September, its net is only 62 percent of our full year forecast," said an OCBC analyst. Conversion $=26.3
